metric.why: A facility can have enough total cooling and still starve individual racks; airflow and pressure sensors find recirculation, bypass, and leaks that temperature averages hide.
metric.definition: Cubic feet per minute delivered through the room or containment system, and the pressure differential that drives it through equipment rather than around it.

reading.body:
Airflow and static pressure reveal whether a data center can actually cool its compute, not just whether it measures cool enough on average.

A facility's total cooling capacity means nothing if air recirculates around equipment or leaks past containment. Racks starved of fresh airflow run hot regardless of how cold the room average reads. Static pressure tracks whether air moves through the servers or bypasses them entirely. This matters because modern AI hardware generates extreme heat density. A pressure drop across the facility shows the cooling system works as designed. Without it, temperatures spike at the point of use, throttling performance or triggering thermal shutdown, even when aggregate data suggests adequate cooling.

This metric does not measure actual chip temperature, coolant performance, or total heat removal. It does not show whether the airflow rate is sufficient for the specific workload or hardware type running. It captures the mechanics of delivery, not the outcome.
